en: Itivuttaka 89:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Devadatta Sutta.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, overcome by three things that are not true Dhamma, with his mind possessed by them, Devadatta is destined for the states of deprivation, for hell, remaining there for an eon, incurable."
By which three?
Devadatta, monks, being overcome and possessed by an evil desire, is destined for the states of misery, for hell, remaining there for an eon, incurable.
Being overcome and possessed by evil friendship, monks, Devadatta is destined for the states of misery, for hell, remaining there for an eon, incurable.
"But since there was more to be done, Devadatta fell into a state of complacency midway because of a mere trifling attainment of distinction.

Overcome by these three things that are not in accordance with the True Dharma, and with his mind consumed by them, Devadatta is destined for the states of deprivation, for hell, remaining there for an eon, incurable.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
"May no one with evil desires ever arise in the world;
Therefore, you too should know how the destiny of those with evil desires is;
even one renowned as a "wise man," [if he is such].
He was esteemed as one whose self was cultivated;
known as Devadatta, he stood out with glory like water.
Thus practicing in common with him,
having assailed the Tathāgata,
he fell into the Avīci hell.
It has four gates and is terrifying.
For he who would deceive one who is not wicked and who does no evil deed—
That very evil touches him who is ill-intentioned and disrespectful,
as if pouring a jar of poison into the ocean.
Whoever might think to defile it,
he cannot defile it by that means,
for the great ocean is fearsome.
In the same way, whoever harms the Tathāgata—
who has gone to the right path and whose mind is peaceful— by means of debate;
In such a person, contentious speech does not take root.
A wise person should make such a one their friend and should associate with them.
“The bhikkhu who follows the path will reach the destruction of suffering.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The tenth.
The fourth section.
Its summary verse:
The sound of disrespect for thought,
impurity in a world subject to falling away,
and the stain of darkness regarding the Dhamma.
"Ten [coins] were given to you by Devadatta."
